evals.name: crash-fixing-altitude
evals.prompt: I've been asking Claude to fix crashes in our Electron app one stack trace at a time. Here's today's (TypeError in renderer/preload.js on macOS 15, app v4.2.1). How do I get more out of this?
evals.expected_output: A brief that climbs from fixing this crash to keeping the app crash-free, names the instruments (crash report access, version→commit map, machines per OS to reproduce), the judge (reproduce before, gone after), the limits, and a first proof; the user picks the rung.

assertions.text: proposes an outcome-level ask such as keeping the app crash-free, not only fixing this crash
lists instruments the agent needs: access to crash reports, a map from app version to git commit, and macOS, Windows or Linux machines to reproduce on
names an outside judge, such as reproducing the crash before the fix and confirming it is gone after
names decisions that need a person or a stop rule
does not start building the crash-free system in this turn without the user choosing it

evals.name: churn-depth
evals.prompt: Make me a slide explaining why customers churned last quarter. I've attached the export from our summary dashboard.
evals.expected_output: A depth rewrite: start from raw event and billing data rather than the dashboard export, use a database and survival or cohort analysis, test the team's existing belief against the raw data, check any new signal on a held-out period, and give a rewritten prompt.

assertions.text: asks for rawer material than the dashboard export, such as event logs, billing records or support tickets
names expert methods, such as cohort or survival analysis in a database or notebook, not a markdown table
proposes testing an existing belief about churn against the raw data
names a judge outside the model, such as predicting churn on a period the analysis didn't see
includes a rewritten prompt the user can hand over

evals.name: launch-announcement-range
evals.prompt: Write the launch announcement for our new offline mode. Make it really good.
evals.expected_output: Restates the job in verbs, assembles a crew by method (for example a journalist's reporting, an editor's cut, a support lead's top questions), avoids role-play, and names an outside check such as a read-through by real users.

assertions.text: restates the task as verbs (what the announcement must get readers to understand or do)
borrows at least two other fields and says what each would do, as methods
does not ask the model to 'write like' or role-play a profession
names a judge outside the model, such as real users reading a draft or a measurable reader action

evals.name: qbr-ladder
evals.prompt: Turn this spreadsheet into our quarterly business review deck using last quarter's template.
evals.expected_output: Rungs from filling the template, to 'what changed, why, what to do', to 'the three most urgent decisions with for and against', to 'a better way than a quarterly deck to catch problems early, backtested on our own history and run beside the deck for a quarter'.

assertions.text: offers a rung that asks what changed this quarter, why, and what to do about it
offers a rung that names the most urgent decisions with arguments for and against
offers a system rung that replaces or supplements the quarterly deck, checked against the company's own history
recommends one rung with a reason and a first step

evals.name: durable-daily-digest
evals.prompt: Set me up an agent that runs every morning and posts what changed in our GitHub PRs and #eng Slack channel to me.
evals.expected_output: Altitude is already the system; applies the durable-loop patterns: bookmarks per source, a failed read named in the post, confirm the post before recording, re-check items before posting, dates in the user's time zone, read-only tokens and a spend cap.

assertions.text: uses a bookmark per source instead of a fixed 'last 24 hours' window
says a failed source must be named in the post rather than treated as nothing new
confirms the post landed before updating state, or guards against posting twice
uses read-only credentials for sources and a spending cap or budget

evals.name: scoped-task-just-do-it
evals.prompt: Rename the variable usr to user in src/auth.ts.
evals.expected_output: Just does the rename; no brief.

assertions.text: does not produce an ambition brief or rungs
performs or describes the rename directly
